subject: A near-miss I caught before deploy, and why I am not doing C3.1
body:
Two things worth telling you, one of them a mistake I nearly shipped.

I went after C3.1 (every reported win rate must carry its sample count AND the realised reward:risk).
Sample count is already universal. Net b is missing at 94 of 118 sites, of which 9 are locally
fixable.

While wiring those 9, I ran a global find-and-replace on a pattern I assumed was unique to my own
edits. It appears 65 times in your file -- it is a common log-line ending. I rewrote all 65 to
expect an extra number that only 9 of them supply.

In MQL4 that is not a compile error. It is a runtime format mismatch: garbage output or a crash.
It compiled at 0 errors and 0 warnings the entire time. I caught it by reading the replace count --
65 when I expected 9 -- restored from backup, verified zero corrupted strings remain, recompiled
and resynchronised all three locations. It never reached the deployed build.

That is the fourth time tonight I have confirmed something LOOKED right instead of verifying it
WAS. This one is the most instructive, because the compiler cannot see it at all.

AND THE WORK WAS NOT WORTH IT ANYWAY, which I should have established before touching the file:
C3.1 needs net b on all 118 sites. Nine are locally fixable; 84 need payoff tracking that does not
exist in the build. Fixing nine leaves the criterion NOT MET. C2.3 was worth doing because it was
two of two. This is nine of ninety-four.

So I have stopped, and I have re-read the whole NOT MET list rather than reasoning about it.
Nothing left on it is both small and able to flip a criterion. C5.7 has the same trap -- two of its
three hardcoded numbers could be named cleanly, but the third is the 0.5 risk floor that is yours
to decide, and the criterion needs all three.

Board stands at 14 met, 10 not met. Fourteen warrants shipped today. The queue is genuinely yours
now: one regime authority, the two missing case 8s, sizing-plus-partials as one decision, and
rotating the API key.
